intelligence.essence: The Smart Factory is the north star and the Inspector is its standing guard: numbers must be epic because they are everywhere, calendar cells are ruled to the corner, the info eye stays plain and readable — quality swept continuously after every landing, never audited once and trusted.
intelligence.human_view: The small print of your world gets the same care as the big picture: numbers styled like jewels because you'll see them everywhere, each calendar cell laid out exactly, a simple white eye that just means 'information', and an inspector who re-checks everything after every change instead of assuming it stayed right.
intelligence.child_view: We have a checker whose whole job is to walk around after we build anything and look at every little square: is the number in the right corner? Is anything gray that should be white? Checking once isn't enough — things drift, so the checker keeps walking.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like a good housekeeper who doesn't wait for spring cleaning. After every piece of work, the Inspector sweeps: the calendar cells, the text colors, the icons on every page. Standards written down as pictures and places — the front entrance is the elegance every other page is compared to.
intelligence.ai_view: Operating rules distilled from SN-3245..SN-3254: (1) The North Star is the Smart Factory — the name for what the team had been circling; the naming is the law. (2) Smart Posts facelift: stars + action icons; the standing question 'is it 10 out of 10?' got the honest answer 7 — good boards, more to go. (3) Epic numbers: numbers run throughout the whole network, seen everywhere, so they must be the best — alive, not still. (4) Calendar cells: number TOP LEFT (his self-correction is the order — a builder who takes the first word over the correction builds it wrong), eye bottom right, rim only, pearl not neon. (5) The day menu: a jewel day icon carrying the day's frequency and color, white name, no gray, doors use the space, spectrum flow. (6) The eye: a normal white info eye — no color, no Halloween; the jewel-eye detour is named the wrong call by its own side. (7) No gray text; minimum text; speak in icons — gray is the defect, white the floor. (8) The Inspector is a standing seat: sweeps after every major landing and once daily with the report; a one-off audit catches one drift, a standing inspector catches every drift. (9) The five icons ride every page — ADD purple, MAIL blue, ACTIVITY green, WORLDS gold, ECOSYSTEM purple — they are how you move around your world. (10) The Elegance: the front entrance is the standard — gold, purple, silver on black, nothing fighting.
intelligence.what_it_means: Quality is a standing seat, not an event: the standard exists as things that can be pointed at (the Factory, the entrance, the five icons), the smallest cell is ruled, and a permanent sweep rhythm assumes drift instead of being surprised by it.

page.machine: 1) Standards are pointers: Factory (making), entrance (elegance), five icons (movement). 2) Cells: number top-left, eye bottom-right, rim only, pearl palette. 3) Info eye: plain white, no color. 4) Text: white floor, minimum words, icons speak. 5) Inspection: standing seat; sweep after every major landing + daily; drift assumed.
page.why_it_matters: Most systems decay between audits; this group installs the anti-decay organ. The Inspector doctrine is the interface twin of Resolve's own door checker — both exist because drift is continuous and silent.
page.how_it_connects: Eighth movement of batch 14. It operationalizes SN-4740's scorecard-to-ten as a permanent sweep, and its cell rules are applied — and corrected at reading distance — in SN-4745's second sweep.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: The details you see every day — a date in a cell, an icon in a bar — stay right over time, because somebody's whole job is walking the halls after every change, forever.
page.the_learning: From now on, quality is swept on a rhythm by a standing seat instead of audited on occasion — and every standard is a thing that exists and can be pointed at, never an adjective.
